title: Elan Group Partners With Marriott to Bring JW Marriott Hotel and Residences to Gurugram
excerpt: The licensing and management deal will add a JW Marriott hotel and branded luxury residences to a 50-acre integrated township on Dwarka Expressway, as India's branded housing market surges.
body:
• Elan Group has signed a licensing and management agreement with Marriott International to develop a JW Marriott Hotel and JW Marriott Residences at Sector 106, Dwarka Expressway, Gurugram.
  • The development will feature 3, 4, and 5 BHK luxury homes within Elan’s approximately 50-acre integrated township, with Marriott Hotels India managing both hotel and residences upon completion.
  • The deal deepens the branded residences trend in Delhi-NCR, where Gurugram has overtaken Mumbai in ultra-luxury home sales above ₹10 crore.
  • India is now the world’s sixth-largest market for branded residences, with a projected 200 per cent increase in such projects by 2031.

Gurugram-based developer Elan Group has signed a licensing and management agreement with Marriott International to introduce a JW Marriott Hotel and JW Marriott Residences within its flagship 50-acre integrated township at Sector 106 on the Dwarka Expressway. The deal brings one of global hospitality’s most recognised luxury brands to one of Delhi-NCR’s fastest-developing corridors.

The development will feature the JW Marriott Hotel Gurugram alongside an exclusive collection of 3, 4, and 5 BHK luxury residences. Elan Group will handle construction and development, while Marriott Hotels India Private Limited will manage both the hotel and residential components upon completion. Sales and marketing for the branded residences will begin after the project obtains the requisite RERA registrations, according to the companies.

“Bringing the JW Marriott brand to our flagship development is driven by a singular purpose—to give our customers and homeowners the privilege of experiencing the impeccable hospitality, intuitive service, world-class amenities and timeless elegance that define JW Marriott, every single day.”

— Ravish Kapoor, Managing Director, Elan Group

A Strategic Corridor for Luxury Development

The Dwarka Expressway location in Sector 106 offers connectivity to Delhi, Indira Gandhi International Airport, and Gurugram’s major business districts—a combination that has made the corridor one of Delhi-NCR’s most active luxury micro-markets. According to JLL, the region recorded more than 13,600 residential launches in the first quarter of 2026 alone, with Dwarka Expressway among the corridors seeing the deepest luxury demand.

Elan Group’s portfolio spans 15 developments across Delhi-NCR with a total built-up area of approximately 25 million square feet. The company did not disclose the number of hotel keys or residential units in the project.

Branded Residences Boom Across India

The Elan-Marriott deal is part of a broader surge in global hospitality brands partnering with Indian developers. India is now the world’s sixth-largest market for branded residences, accounting for 4 per cent of global supply, according to Savills. The segment is expected to see a 200 per cent increase by 2031, with Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Pune accounting for more than 70 per cent of all projects under development.

Branded residences typically command a 20 to 40 per cent price premium over non-branded luxury homes and tend to appreciate faster due to limited inventory and brand value. In Delhi-NCR alone, several developers including M3M Group, Signature Global, Whiteland Corporation, and Gulshan Group have entered the branded homes segment in recent years.

Gurugram’s luxury credentials have strengthened rapidly. According to India Sotheby’s International Realty and CRE Matrix, the city overtook Mumbai in sales of ultra-luxury homes priced at ₹10 crore and above in 2025, with high-end home sales surging 80 per cent year-on-year to ₹24,120 crore.

“This signing represents an important milestone in Marriott International’s continued expansion in one of the world’s most dynamic luxury markets.”

— Rajeev Menon, President – Asia Pacific (excluding China), Marriott International

What It Means for NRI Investors

For diaspora families considering real estate in India, branded residences have emerged as a compelling proposition. The JW Marriott name carries instant global recognition, offering NRI buyers a quality benchmark they can trust without needing on-the-ground oversight. Returning NRIs and high-net-worth individuals from the diaspora have been identified as a key buyer segment in the current luxury cycle, drawn to properties that combine lifestyle appeal with long-term value appreciation.

The managed-living model—where Marriott handles day-to-day operations and services—is particularly attractive for overseas buyers who want a premium Indian address without the hassle of remote property management. With branded homes appreciating faster than conventional luxury options, they also serve as a store of value in a market where NCR housing prices have risen more than 80 per cent over the past five years.

What’s Next

The project is in its early stages, with construction to be undertaken by Elan Group and sales awaiting RERA registration. The companies have not announced a timeline for completion or pricing details. As the Dwarka Expressway corridor continues to attract global hospitality and luxury brands, the JW Marriott development is positioned to set a new benchmark for integrated luxury living in Gurugram—and to draw attention from both domestic and diaspora buyers looking for India’s next marquee address.
